tldr: Headlines across 12 national buckets overwhelmingly foreground PM Sanchez's accusation of Russian and Israeli disinformation—at least nine titles lead with that angle—while five others foreground clashes and civil unrest in Ceuta. The 141 deaths and humanitarian emergency that open the body texts are almost entirely invisible at the headline layer, and the Morocco-orchestration question is visible only as a denial.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Uniquely extreme severity register at headline level: 'Rapes and violence a daily occurrence... verge of disaster... worst of the worst' — no other headline across 12 buckets approaches this danger framing.

Only headline in the corpus to avoid Russia's alleged disinformation role entirely, pivoting instead to Morocco's enforcement arrests — the deflection is complete and legible at a single-title glance.
Headline reads only 'Política' (section label) — entirely uninformative at RSS/homepage layer; the story is invisible as a standalone title, a structural silence the body pass cannot detect.

Interrogative framing — 'What triggered the mass migrant crossings into Ceuta?' — is the only headline to avoid asserting a cause or blame, placing this outlet in the silence bucket while all others commit to a frame.

bottom_line: The headline layer reduces the Ceuta crisis to a Russia-Israel information war and a street-violence emergency, erasing both the humanitarian death toll and the ongoing 5,000-person shelter crisis that dominate the body texts.
